title: Free for football
setting: A weekday morning outside the flats. Kenta is running for the 8:15 train when the elderly neighbour, Satou-san, stops him for 'just a minute'. Satou-san takes his time getting to the point.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: うわ、もう八時？時間ない！
lines.kana: うわ、もうはちじ？じかんない！
lines.english: Ugh, eight already? I'm out of time!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, kenta-kun. ohayou gozaimasu. chotto ii desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、ケンタくん。おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.kana: あ、けんたくん。おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.english: Ah, Kenta. Good morning. Have you got a moment?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, satou-san, ohayou gozaimasu. sumimasen, ima chotto jikan ga nai n desu. hachiji juugofun no densha ni noranai to.
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん、おはようございます。すみません、今ちょっと時間がないんです。八時十五分の電車に乗らないと。
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん、おはようございます。すみません、いまちょっとじかんがないんです。はちじじゅうごふんのでんしゃにのらないと。
lines.english: Oh, Satou-san, good morning. Sorry, I don't really have time right now. I've got to catch the 8:15.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ippun de owarimasu yo. nichiyoubi wa hima desu ka?
lines.ja: 一分で終わりますよ。日曜日は暇ですか？
lines.kana: いっぷんでおわりますよ。にちようびはひまですか？
lines.english: It'll only take a minute. Are you free on Sunday?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nichiyoubi desu ka? zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: 日曜日ですか？ずっと仕事が忙しくて、土曜も日曜も暇がないんですよ。
lines.kana: にちようびですか？ずっとしごとがいそがしくて、どようもにちようもひまがないんですよ。
lines.english: Sunday? Work's been crazy for ages. I don't get any free time, Saturday or Sunday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, ima wa yoyuu ga nai n desu ne. nichiyoubi no sakkaa no chiketto ga nimai aru n desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、今は余裕がないんですね。日曜日のサッカーのチケットが二枚あるんですけどね。
lines.kana: ああ、いまはよゆうがないんですね。にちようびのさっかーのちけっとがにまいあるんですけどね。
lines.english: Ah, so you're swamped right now. Only, I've got two tickets for Sunday's football...

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sakkaa? ikitai desu! demo, ima okane nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: え、サッカー？行きたいです！でも、今お金ないんですよ。
lines.kana: え、さっかー？いきたいです！でも、いまおかねないんですよ。
lines.english: Huh, football? I'd love to go! But I'm broke right now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ichimai, gosen en desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: 一枚、五千円ですけどね。
lines.kana: いちまい、ごせんえんですけどね。
lines.english: Well, they're five thousand yen each...

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gosen en kaa. chotto okane ga tarinai desu.
lines.ja: 五千円かあ。ちょっとお金が足りないです。
lines.kana: ごせんえんかあ。ちょっとおかねがたりないです。
lines.english: Five thousand, huh. I'm a bit short.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: okane ga tarinai? iya iya, kenta-kun, okane wa ii n desu yo.
lines.ja: お金が足りない？いやいや、ケンタくん、お金はいいんですよ。
lines.kana: おかねがたりない？いやいや、けんたくん、おかねはいいんですよ。
lines.english: Short? No, no, Kenta. You don't need to pay.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, ii n desu ka? ima honto ni okane no yoyuu ga nakute.
lines.ja: え、いいんですか？今ほんとにお金の余裕がなくて。
lines.kana: え、いいんですか？いまほんとにおかねのよゆうがなくて。
lines.english: What, really? Money's really tight right now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii n desu yo. watashi mo mukashi wa, okane ga nakatta desu kara.
lines.ja: いいんですよ。私も昔は、お金がなかったですから。
lines.kana: いいんですよ。わたしもむかしは、おかねがなかったですから。
lines.english: It's fine. I was broke too, back in the day.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、ほんとにありがとうございます！
lines.kana: さとうさん、ほんとにありがとうございます！

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, kenta-kun, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n deshou?
lines.ja: でも、ケンタくん、土曜も日曜も暇がないんでしょう？
lines.kana: でも、けんたくん、どようもにちようもひまがないんでしょう？
lines.english: But Kenta, I thought you had no free time, Saturday or Sunday?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: いや、サッカーなら暇あります！
lines.kana: いや、さっかーならひまあります！

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hahaha. watashi wa ikanai node, sora-kun to douzo.
lines.ja: ははは。私は行かないので、ソラくんとどうぞ。
lines.kana: ははは。わたしはいかないので、そらくんとどうぞ。
lines.english: Ha ha ha. I'm not going, so take Sora with you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai! a, mou hachiji juppun! jikan nai! itte kimasu!
lines.ja: はい！あ、もう八時十分！時間ない！行ってきます！
lines.kana: はい！あ、もうはちじじゅっぷん！じかんない！いってきます！
lines.english: Will do! Oh, it's ten past eight already! I'm out of time! I'm off!

choices.english: Satou-san invites Kenta to Sunday's football, but Kenta can't afford a ticket, so he says no.
Kenta misses his train because Satou-san wants his help with something on Sunday.
Kenta says he has no free time and no money, but when Satou-san gives him the football tickets for free, he's suddenly free on Sunday.

questions.explanation: Lines 3 and 5: Kenta has no time right now (jikan ga nai) and no free time at weekends (hima ga nai). Line 7: he's broke (okane nai), and line 9: he's a bit short for a 5,000-yen ticket (okane ga tarinai). Line 10: Satou-san says he doesn't need to pay (okane wa ii n desu yo), and in line 16 he says he isn't going himself, so Kenta can take Sora. Line 15: for football, Kenta is suddenly free (sakkaa nara hima arimasu). A is wrong: Kenta can't afford the tickets, but he doesn't have to pay, and he takes them happily. B is wrong: Satou-san only wanted to give him the tickets, and at ten past eight (line 17) Kenta runs off for his 8:15 train. Nobody says he misses it.

questions.english: You're running for your train when Kenta catches you: "ne, ima chotto ii? hanashi ga aru n da kedo." (Hey, got a sec? I need to talk to you.) Tell him you've got no time right now.
questions.ja: ね、今ちょっといい？話があるんだけど。
questions.kana: ね、いまちょっといい？はなしがあるんだけど。
questions.romaji: ne, ima chotto ii? hanashi ga aru n da kedo.
questions.answer: Say you have no time right now with jikan and nai. Kenta's a friend, so keep it casual: gomen, ima jikan nai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ima jikan nai n da. densha ni noranai to.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今時間ないんだ。電車に乗らないと。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I don't have time right now. I've got to catch my train.

modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん！もう時間ない！
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry! I'm out of time!

questions.explanation: Time is something there is or isn't, so it's jikan ga nai, not jikan o motte nai. Kenta says it to himself in line 1 (jikan nai!) and politely to Satou-san in line 3 (ima chotto jikan ga nai n desu). It's about right now, so use jikan, not hima: hima ga nai means no free time these days (line 5). Mou jikan nai is 'I'm out of time', as Kenta says in line 17. With a friend, drop ga and end with n da.

questions.english: Satou-san invites you over: "nichiyoubi, uchi ni kimasen ka?" (Would you like to come over on Sunday?) You've been working every weekend for a month. Apologise and say you've had no free time.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うちに来ませんか？
questions.kana: にちようび、うちにきませんか？
questions.answer: Apologise and say you've got no free time these days, with hima and nai, politely: sumimasen, zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, hima ga nai n desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, hima ga nai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、ずっと仕事が忙しくて、暇がないんです。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, work's been so busy for ages. I've got no free time.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、土曜も日曜も暇がないんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I don't get any free time, Saturday or Sunday.

questions.explanation: hima ga nai means no free time these days. Kenta uses it for his weekends in line 5 (doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo), and Satou-san teases him with the same words in line 14. jikan ga nai is for right now or one thing, like Kenta rushing for the 8:15 in line 3. After a month of working weekends, it's hima. Satou-san is an elderly neighbour, so answer politely with n desu, and say sumimasen first to soften the no.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "ne, ashita kaimono ni ikanai?" (Hey, want to go shopping tomorrow?) It's the end of the month and your bank account is empty. Tell him you're broke.
questions.ja: ね、明日買い物に行かない？
questions.kana: ね、あしたかいものにいかない？
questions.answer: Say you're broke with okane and nai, casually: gomen, ima okane nai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ima okane nai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今お金ないんだ。

modelAnswers.romaji: ikitai kedo, ima okane nai kara, gomen.
modelAnswers.ja: 行きたいけど、今お金ないから、ごめん。
modelAnswers.english: I'd love to, but I'm broke right now, so sorry.

questions.explanation: Being broke is okane (ga) nai. Kenta says it in line 7 (ima okane nai n desu yo), and Satou-san uses the past in line 12 (mukashi wa, okane ga nakatta). Okane o motte nai usually means you have no cash on you right now, not that you're broke. Okane ga tarinai would be short for one thing, like the 5,000-yen ticket in lines 9-10, but here you have no money for anything. Okane nai kara... gives it as the reason.

questions.english: When Satou-san says the tickets are 5,000 yen each, Kenta says "chotto okane ga tarinai desu." What does he mean?
questions.kana: けんたさんのおかねは？

choices.english: He thinks 5,000 yen is too much to pay for a football ticket.
He doesn't have quite enough to pay for a 5,000-yen ticket.
He has no money at all, not even for his train.

questions.explanation: Line 9: okane ga tarinai means the money isn't enough, so he's short for one particular thing, here a 5,000-yen ticket. Chotto tarinai is 'a bit short'. Satou-san repeats it in line 10 (okane ga tarinai?) before telling him he doesn't need to pay. A would be takai (expensive), which nobody says. C goes too far. In line 7 Kenta does say he's broke (ima okane nai), but tarinai only says he can't cover this ticket, and he's still on his way to catch his train (lines 3 and 17).

questions.english: Satou-san says Kenta doesn't need to pay. Kenta is relieved. What does he say about his money?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: ima honto ni okane no yoyuu ga nakute.

choices.english: I really can't 'afford' it right now (English verb)
I really don't hold any money to spare right now
choices.romaji: ima honto ni okane no yoyuu o motte nakute.

questions.explanation: Line 11: okane no yoyuu ga nai means no money to spare, money's tight. The -te form nakute trails off as a reason. In line 6 Satou-san uses yoyuu on its own (ima wa yoyuu ga nai n desu ne), meaning Kenta is swamped, with no time or energy to spare. B is wrong: Japanese has no verb for 'afford', and afoodo isn't a word. For one item you'd say kaenai (can't buy it), and for money in general okane no yoyuu ga nai. C is wrong: like time and money, yoyuu is something there is or isn't, so it takes ga nai, never o motte nai.

newWords.english: counter for flat things like tickets (ichimai = one, nimai = two)
long ago, back in the day
if it's...; when it comes to (sakkaa nara = for football)
